definitions.meaning: a word for any thing whose name escapes you, a thingummy
goings-on, the things people are up to

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal British usage: a gadget whose name you forget, and events or happenings.

clue.text: Lodge in pub with social worker that's outraged

indicators.note: the word lodge is placed inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
digs are lodgings, so to dig is to lodge
the ant is the classic social insect, and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: Someone staying above a pub with a social worker is furious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' reads as a council employee but is the crossword ant, an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indignant is feeling anger at unfair treatment, a synonym for being outraged.

clue.text: Pretty little cave reached round river

indicators.note: the phrase for reached goes round the abbreviation for river

parts.note: got to means reached

explanation.surface: Walkers find a charming small cave after following a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cavern, often ornamental, so a pretty little cave fits.

clue.text: Give actor something of a hand -is it a date?

parts.note: the palm is part of the hand
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether applauding an actor counts as a romantic evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ... a hand' suggests applause; 'date' suggests romance but is the fruit, which grows on one kind of palm.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates grow on the date palm, so asking whether a tree is a date tree describes a palm.

clue.text: Israel's measure

definitions.meaning: An ancient port city in northern Israel
a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a historic Israeli city on the Mediterranean, the other a land-area unit used in Britain and the US.

clue.text: Scotsman willing to be a theatre manager

parts.note: Mac, from the common surname prefix, is a familiar name for a Scotsman
ready means willing or prepared to be

explanation.surface: A Scot is keen to take on running a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: William Charles Macready was the great Victorian actor-manager of Covent Garden and Drury Lane.
explanation.definitionFit: William Macready managed both Covent Garden and Drury Lane theatres in the 1830s and 1840s.

clue.text: Shakespearean philosopher losing house in proportion

indicators.note: the philosopher's name drops the abbreviation for house

parts.note: Horatio is Hamlet's scholarly friend, told there are more things than are dreamt of in his philosophy

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character ends up homeless, but keeps a sense of balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relative size of two quantities, the same as a proportion.

clue.text: Cave in kitchen garden

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words kitchen garden

explanation.surface: Someone has dug a cave within the vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is not a cavern but the Latin warning 'beware!', used by English schoolboys.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are warnings: the Latin cry 'look out' and the fencer's call to be on guard.

clue.text: The latest from the poker game?

definitions.text: The latest from the poker game?

parts.words: The latest from the poker game?
parts.note: the freshest news, read also as the state of a fire poker that has been in the flames, glowing hot

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the newest gossip from the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: The card game is a red herring: the poker is a fireside iron, and very fresh news is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Very recent news is described as hot off the press, and an iron left in the fire glows with heat.

clue.text: Great little picture demands valuation

indicators.note: the letters are made to work, rearranged to the setter's demand

parts.note: pic is a short form of picture

explanation.surface: A fine small painting calls for an expert appraisal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' signals the rearrangement of GREAT with PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A price label states what an item is worth, its value as set by the seller.

explanation.surface: A politician hands back a firearm and the gesture achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no worth or effect, synonymous with worthless.

clue.text: Enlarged route badly routed

indicators.note: the letters of routed are put together badly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lengthened path was poorly planned.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion takes a longer way round, so it is an extended road.

clue.text: Cheese produced with backing

indicators.note: the word for produced runs backwards

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: Cheese is manufactured with financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese with a red wax coat.

clue.text: What can't be eaten without some cream can't be swallowed

indicators.note: here 'without' means outside, so the inedible word goes round

parts.note: inedible describes food that can't be eaten

indicators.note: only some of the word cream is used, its opening pair

explanation.surface: Food that is unfit to eat, with a bit of cream, still won't go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, its old sense, not lacking; CR is the start of cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that can't be swallowed is not believable, the figurative sense of swallow.

clue.text: Good book about traditional form of garden structure

indicators.note: the scripture goes about the other piece

parts.note: the Good Book is the Bible

indicators.note: a new form of the word means it is rearranged

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz

explanation.surface: A Bible discusses old-fashioned designs for garden buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but means the scripture goes around the reworked letters; 'form of' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for feeding wild birds stands in many gardens.

clue.text: Rocks increase exponentially ie rocks with drinks on

parts.note: drinks served on the rocks come with ice
to cube a number is to raise it to the third power

explanation.surface: A geological note about rocks multiplying, then a bar note about drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ie' introduces the definition: the rocks a drink is served on.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky on the rocks is served over frozen blocks, so these are the rocks drinks sit on.

clue.text: Ancestor, perhaps, with relative to follow

definitions.meaning: a forebear, one who came before
in grammar, the noun that a relative pronoun such as who or which refers back to

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean something that comes before: a forebear, and the noun preceding a relative pronoun.

clue.text: Effect of devil's performance

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A demon's stage turn makes an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: The impact of something is its influence or result.

clue.text: Malfunctioning part of gas lit church

indicators.note: just the first letter of gas is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty piece of gas lighting in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective standing for the noun: a glitch is a malfunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden fault, a brief failure to work properly.

clue.text: Instinctive part of ten thousand, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: in Freud the id is the instinctive part of the mind
10 written as the letters I and O
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A remark that something is instinctively part of ten thousand, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression, a turn of phrase.

clue.text: Lorry-driver's mate with rest disturbed

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the lorry-driver

indicators.note: the letters of mate and rest are disturbed, mixed up

explanation.surface: A trucker's companion has his sleep interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a teamster is a truck driver, after the Teamsters union.

clue.text: Time on river with J. George, and Harris?

indicators.note: in a down clue the time sits on top of the river

parts.note: rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river

explanation.surface: Time spent on the river with the three men of the comic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: J, George and Harris are the boaters of Jerome K. Jerome's 'Three Men in a Boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Three companions are a threesome.

clue.text: Artist during time in gaol making a weathercock, possibly

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
in means during
bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime, is a prison sentence

explanation.surface: An artist in prison makes a weathervane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time in prison. A rainbird, such as the green woodpecker, is said to foretell rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird whose call is thought to predict rain acts as a living weather forecaster.

clue.text: Profits of student fund-raising -all sorts of things

parts.note: rag week is British students' annual charity fundraising
a bag is a haul or take, the proceeds

explanation.surface: The takings from a students' charity event are a varied collection.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is British students' annual charity event; the BAG is its haul.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a jumbled mixture of miscellaneous items.

clue.text: Pantomime featuring posh young doctors in boat

indicators.note: the posh and the doctors go inside the boat

parts.note: a dhow is an Arab sailing boat
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a newly qualified doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A pantomime with posh trainee medics on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb show is acting in mime, without words.

clue.text: Be there and listen — a dry conclusion

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: Advice to turn up and pay heed, then a dry ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is both to be present and to pay attention.
